weaknesses.critique: The claim asks whether operating margin 'exceeded 25%' and the evidence shows 28.7%. While this clearly exceeds 25%, I should verify this is not affected by rounding. The computed figure shows 0.28706117936630443 (28.706%), which when rounded to one decimal place gives 28.7%. This confirms the margin genuinely exceeds 25% and is not a borderline case where rounding could affect the conclusion.

The evidence (E2) notes that the operating margin increase was 'primarily driven by lower other operating charges, due to the prior year remeasurement of our contingent consideration liability to fair value in conjunction with the fairlife acquisition.' This suggests that a significant portion of the margin improvement from 21.2% in 2024 to 28.7% in 2025 may be due to one-time or non-recurring items in the prior year. However, the claim only asks whether the 2025 margin exceeded 25%, not whether it was driven by sustainable operational improvements, so this does not contradict the claim as stated.

I should confirm that 'fiscal year 2025' aligns with the period ended December 31, 2025 shown in the evidence. The evidence E2 is from a 10-K filed 2026-02-20 for period ending 2025-12-31, which represents Coca-Cola's full fiscal year 2025. This matches the claim's reference to 'fiscal year 2025', so there is no period mismatch issue.
